subject: Scout AI inference economics readout & next actions
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reed <tom@scoutai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Scout AI inference economics readout & next actions

Tom — thanks again for a crisp discovery call this morning. Quick readout from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum. I kept the math high-level; we can send the raw runs once we complete the validation tests.

High-level per-1M token cost (illustrative, includes serving + infra amortized):
- Redwood (default config, mixed-quant): ~$8.50 / 1M tokens
- AWS Bedrock (comparable model family): ~$12.60 / 1M tokens
- GCP Vertex AI endpoints: ~$11.20 / 1M tokens

What drove the delta: networking + optimized kernels in our runtime, automatic KV/prefix caching (saves tokens on multi-turn workflows), and continuous batching behavior for small requests.

Key sensitivity notes for Scout workload (what we heard on the call):
- Short multi-turn chat (avg. 18 tokens per user turn), high rate of repeated prompts across user sessions
- Peak concurrency target: ~250 QPS, median 40 QPS
- Quality bar: near-production Llama-2 style performance (we'll match model family)

What we'd like to run next (proposed test matrix):
1) 1M-token synthetic replay of your sample dataset (measure per-token cost across Redwood/AWS/GCP). Owner: Redwood. Target: 2026-08-14
2) Batching sensitivity sweep: evaluate token-level batching at batch sizes [1,8,32] and report cost and p95 latency. Owner: Redwood infra + Ben. Target: 2026-08-16
3) Cache-warm vs cold runs: measure prefix/KV cache hit rate impact (we expect your current hit ~18%; with prefix caching we typically move to ~35–40%). Owner: Scout provides sample queries; Redwood runs tests. Deliverable: hit-rate / cost curves. Target: 2026-08-18
4) Quality A/B: identical prompts, compare top-k output similarity and any downstream metric you care about (F1 / human pass). Owner: Scout + Redwood. Target: schedule week of 8/24

Immediate asks from us (small list):
- Please share a 10–20 prompt sample set (anonymized) and a representative 30-minute traffic dump (metadata only). Email to me or upload to the Drive link below.
- Confirm preferred time window for the 1M-token run (we can run in your region to minimize egress).

Attachments: scout_econ_summary.pdf (high-level math + assumptions).

If that plan looks good we'll: 1) queue the 1M-token synthetic run, 2) send a scoped mutual action plan (timeline + owners), and 3) prepare a short SOC2 evidence packet to help procurement.

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz

Nice summary Vanessa — a couple of quick internal asks before we kick off runs: 
- Can we capture both tokenized OS-level counts (input + output) and normalized user-facing tokens so Scout can reconcile with their billing?
- Add a run with 95th-percentile context length from their sample (you mentioned bursts to 512 tokens). We should surface how much longer contexts affect both latency and cost.

I'll slot Ben for the batching sweep; I'll own the Drive folder and the SOC2 stub prep.

Also — let's make sure the synthetic replay includes a session-level randomness seed so we don't inadvertently leak PII if any sample has edge tokens. We should sanitize on receipt.

Laura

Thanks — here's what I'll run and deliver:
- Batching sweep (batch sizes 1/8/32) across three concurrency points (20 QPS / 100 QPS / 250 QPS). Will report per-1M-token cost, p50/p95 latency, and GPU utilization.
- Cache warm vs cold: two runs for each concurrency point to estimate cache hit delta and effect on cost.

Pricing question for the commercial thread: if Scout wants a committed capacity discount (monthly commit), we should model a simple uplift to the per-1M number (e.g., 10% off at $100k/mo commitment, 18% off at $250k/mo). I'll attach a rough MSP estimate to frame procurement conversations.
